# Mock handoff — what pozo (Rol 1) and fradiaz (Rol 2) can rely on tonight

**Status:** mock artefacts generated by `pipeline/generate_mock.py`, contract `1.0`, fingerprint
`049376b0…`. Verify any copy you receive with `./scripts/check_phase_a.sh`.

Read `docs/data-contract-v1.md` only if you need the normative detail. This page is the short
version plus the four things that will bite you.

---

## 1. What you get

One directory per case under `data/processed/`:

```
data/processed/{case}/nisar_grid.parquet      # one row per H3 res-9 cell
data/processed/{case}/timeseries.csv          # one row per date for the case aggregate
data/processed/{case}/context_layers.geojson  # land use, infrastructure, water, boundaries
data/processed/{case}/meta.json               # dates, thresholds, provenance, stats, limitations
data/processed/_availability/{case}.json      # source-probe evidence; not a case — case glob is */nisar_grid.parquet
```

Cases: `mexico-city`, `jakarta`, `malaga`. Loaders are Rol 1's: `src/data/loaders.py` does not exist
in the tree yet, so copy the reference instead of re-translating this page —
`examples/reference_loader.py` is the working version of §2b, and it imports nothing from
`examples/` (only `src.domain.contracts`), so the copy is the whole install:

```bash
mkdir -p src/data && cp examples/reference_loader.py src/data/loaders.py
```

Run from the repo root: that is what puts `src.domain.contracts` on `sys.path`, and `load_case`
resolves `data/processed` against the cwd, not against the module's own directory. Nothing here
imports Streamlit and nothing needs NASA credentials.

### What the current mock actually contains (seed 7, 2026-11-14)

| case | cells | median mm/yr | p05 | coherence | land-use classes | size |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|
| `mexico-city` | 11,694 | −62.1 | −231.9 | 0.44–0.95 | 6 | 0.86 MB |
| `jakarta` | 4,811 | −25.4 | −141.9 | 0.35–0.95 | 6 | 0.38 MB |
| `malaga` | 2,645 | −1.4 | −3.5 | 0.35–0.95 | 6 | 0.22 MB |

The published cells are the AOI's **bbox** ∩ the coverage ellipse, and the `admin_boundary` polygon is that
ellipse: **12 / 5 / 2** published cells (Mexico City / Jakarta / Málaga) lie outside its ring, so clipping to
it counts **11,682** instead of **11,694** in Mexico City; trust the grid counts. The QGIS ring in
`config/aoi/{case}.geojson` is much tighter than that footprint — only 6,620 / 3,873 / 2,051 published cells
fall inside it — so clipping to it is a real filter, not a rounding.

Two changes since the first cut, both deliberate — if your numbers differ, you are reading a stale copy:

- **Water cells are absent from the grid.** A specular surface has no usable phase, so the quality
  filter drops those cells (the contract's nodata rule: absent, never 0). The coastline, lake and
  river are still in `context_layers.geojson` as `layer: "water"` features, so the map can draw the
  coast without publishing "ocean with subsidence". That is also why `land_use` shows 6 classes in
  the grid instead of 7.
- **The seasonal harmonic is centred on the window.** It used to be anchored at the first date,
  which over a 132-day window made the seasonal term masquerade as subsidence: `delta_change/T`
  overstated the trend by 2–8×, and hundreds of cells rose in the map while falling in the slider.
  Now both endpoints carry the same seasonal offset, so `delta_change` tracks `velocity_mm_yr`
  exactly (verified: median ratio 1.000, zero sign disagreements in all three cases). The seasonal
  bulge is still visible mid-window; it is a dip-and-return, not a ramp.
- **Coherence is no longer clipped up to 0.45.** Modelled coherence now reaches the frozen threshold
  (0.35), so the coherence filter removes cells instead of being a no-op on land: Jakarta
  5,000 → 4,811 and Málaga 3,647 → 2,645 cells, and every published cell satisfies
  `coherence ≥ 0.35`.

Water is context, not a grid class, and differs by case: `reservoir` + `river` (Mexico City), `coastline` +
`canal` (Jakarta), `coastline` + `river` (Málaga). `water` and `unknown` never appear in the grid's `land_use` — cells are dropped, not relabelled.

All three: 12 dates, `2026-07-02 → 2026-11-11`, `product = mock`, `revisit_days = 12`,
`cell_id == "aoi"` series starting at 0 mm. If a number you see is wildly off this table, you are
probably reading a stale copy — regenerate with `./scripts/python.sh pipeline/generate_mock.py`
or check it with `./scripts/check_phase_a.sh`.

## 2. Columns you can bind to

**Grid** — `cell_id` (H3 string, unique), `lat`, `lon` (WGS84 centroid), `val_t1`, `val_t2`,
`delta_change` (mm, cumulative, up-positive), `velocity_mm_yr` (mm/yr, **this is the colourable
metric**), `coherence` (0–1), `land_use`, `risk_level`, `case_id`, `sensor`, `product`, `unit`,
`velocity_unit`, `source`, `acquisition_date`, `provenance_id`.

**Map bindings** (T = 132 days = 0.36140 yr, from 132/365.25 = 0.3613963):

| visual | column | unit |
|---|---|---|
| colour | `velocity_mm_yr` | mm/yr |
| height | `delta_change` | mm |
| category | `land_use` | — |
| risk | `risk_level` | — |
| time constant | T = 0.36140 | yr |

`delta_change = velocity_mm_yr × 0.36140` (max residual 0.002 mm); `delta_change/T ÷ velocity_mm_yr
= 1.000` (0.99999 at 5 dp) for every published cell.

**Series** — `case_id`, `cell_id`, `date`, `value` (mm), `unit`, `sensor`, `product`, `quality`,
`provenance_id`. Chart the rows where `cell_id == "aoi"`; per-cell rows only exist if the artefact
was generated with `--per-cell-series`.

**Enums you will actually render**: `land_use` ∈ urban-dense, urban-residential, industrial,
infrastructure, water, bare, vegetation, unknown · `risk_level` ∈ estable, moderado, critico ·
`quality` ∈ good, fair, poor.

**Risk bands** (from `contracts.risk_level_from_velocity`, sign-agnostic magnitude bands): `estable`
|v| < 5, `moderado` 5 ≤ |v| < 25, `critico` |v| ≥ 25 mm/yr — for these negative velocities, v > −5,
−25 < v ≤ −5, v ≤ −25. The flat-case trigger (`NULL_RESULT_MM_YR = 5`) also uses 5 but is unrelated
(`estable` is per-cell, the trigger per-case).

**Dtypes and nodata.** String: `cell_id`, `land_use`, `risk_level`, `case_id`, `sensor`, `product`,
`unit`, `velocity_unit`, `source`, `acquisition_date`, `provenance_id` (pandas 3.x reports `str`,
2.x `object` — do not assert on the dtype object). Float64: `lat`, `lon`, `val_t1`, `val_t2`,
`delta_change`, `velocity_mm_yr`, `coherence`. Dates are ISO-8601 without timezone; `acquisition_date` is a constant equal to the last date (`2026-11-11`), not per-cell.

## 2b. The loader API — what `src/data/loaders.py` returns

Copy `examples/reference_loader.py` (the working version of this page) and this is exactly what you
get:

```python
from reference_loader import load_case, grid_frame, map_payload, aoi_series, kpis

case = load_case("mexico-city")                                    # Case; validates on load, fails closed
case = load_case("mexico-city", processed="/srv/data/processed")   # or pass the artefact root
grid = grid_frame(case)                                            # DataFrame copy, dtypes asserted
rows = map_payload(case, coherence_min=0.6, land_use=["urban-dense", "urban-residential"])
dates, values = aoi_series(case)                                   # (list[str], list[float]) in mm
cards = kpis(case)                                                 # dict, copied from meta.stats
```

- **`load_case(case_id, processed=None)`** → a `Case` carrying `case_id`, `grid`, `series`, `meta`,
  `context`, `path`. `processed` defaults to `data/processed` under the **caller's cwd**, and a
  relative value resolves there too — never against the module's `__file__`. So **run from the repo
  root or pass `processed=`**: a copy that sits one directory down otherwise looks for a tree that
  is not there and raises, naming the path it tried. Missing artefact, undeclared enum, broken
  invariant: `LoaderError`, never an empty frame.
- **`grid_frame(case)`** → a fresh `DataFrame` copy (mutate it freely), dtypes re-asserted per §2.
- **`map_payload(case, *, coherence_min=None, land_use=None, risk_level=None)`** → **one dict per
  published cell, exactly seven keys**: `lat`, `lon`, `cell_id`, `color_value`, `height`,
  `category`, `risk` — one dict *per cell*, not one dict for the whole map, and not a DataFrame.
  Bindings are the §2 table, values are the stored floats **verbatim**: nothing recomputed, nothing
  rounded (`color_value` is `velocity_mm_yr`, `height` is `delta_change`). `coherence_min` is
  inclusive; row order is the artefact's.
- **Filters are ANDed and only REMOVE rows.** Nodata is absent, so a filter that matches nothing
  **raises** `LoaderError` naming the filter and the case — never `[]`, never `fillna(0)`. An empty
  list, an undeclared enum value or a `coherence_min` outside `[0, 1]` raises too.
- **`aoi_series(case, *, chart_unit="mm")`** → `(dates, values)`: `meta.dates` as `str` and the stored
  `cell_id == "aoi"` values in mm, in that order, starting at 0. `chart_unit` accepts only `"mm"`;
  convert for display in the component, never here.
- **`kpis(case)`** → a `dict` copied from `meta.json`: `cells`, `median_velocity_mm_yr`, `p05`,
  `p95`, `spread` (`p95 − p05`), `dates`, `window_days`, `product`, `provenance_id`, plus
  `coverage_fraction` and `detection_limit_mm_yr` **when `meta.stats` publishes them**. Málaga
  carries the **configured mock value** `detection_limit_mm_yr = 1.5` with
  `median_velocity_mm_yr = −1.358`, so `|median| < limit` is a card you can render:
  **"below detection"**, not a dash. The 1.5 is not estimated from mock residuals. Mexico City and
  Jakarta do not publish the key, so it is *absent* there — absent means "not a flat case", not
  "unknown".
- **Nothing is recomputed**: colour is `velocity_mm_yr` as stored, height `delta_change` as stored,
  the chart the stored `aoi` rows, the KPIs `meta.stats`. No smoothing, interpolation or unit
  conversion.

## 3. Four things that will bite you

1. **Nodata is absent, not zero.** A cell with no data is missing from the grid, and a date with no
   data is missing from the series. Never `fillna(0)` — in Málaga zero is a real velocity, and
   filling destroys the one scientific point the demo makes.
2. **`delta_change` and `velocity_mm_yr` are different quantities.** Slider delta is mm; the map
   colour is mm/yr. Mixing them is the easiest way to publish a wrong number.
   `val_t1` is **exactly 0 for every cell by construction** — cumulative displacement is referenced
   to the first acquisition, so the slider shows change *since that date*, not an absolute level.
   That is deliberate, not a bug: do not "fix" it by re-adding an offset.
3. **`product` is `mock` and `provenance.source` says so.** Render the badge. This is deliberate:
   the identical schema will later carry real data, and only `meta.json` will change.
4. **Málaga is flat on purpose.** `|median velocity| < 5 mm/yr` ⇒ `stats.detection_limit_mm_yr`
   is mandatory (`1.5`) and `kpis()` surfaces it as `cards["detection_limit_mm_yr"]` (§2b). Show
  "below detection", not "no data" and not "stable, all good": the KPI can express the null result,
  so a missing card is the bug.

## 3b. Shared vs independent legend

Do not hardcode a legend. These per-case percentiles are what the **independent** toggle uses —
read them from `meta.stats`, never from this table:

| case | p05 | p95 | spread |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `mexico-city` | −231.9 | −22.7 | 209.2 |
| `jakarta` | −141.9 | 2.7 | 144.5 |
| `malaga` | −3.5 | 0.7 | 4.2 |

**Do not clip the shared scale at p05/p95.** That range (−231.9 … 2.7 mm/yr) would hide Mexico
City's core, whose cells reach **−415.1 mm/yr** — the bowl would saturate and the strongest signal
in the demo would render flat-topped. Use a **symmetric scale about 0 at ±425 mm/yr**: the contrast
survives (Mexico City's spread is still **50.3×** Málaga's), the extreme cells stay visible, and no
panel needs clipping. `docs/figures/velocity_shared_scale.png` uses exactly this scale, so the app
and the pitch figure agree.

The independent per-case toggle may use each city's own p05/p95 — offer it as a comparison, never
as the default, or the contrast disappears.

## 3c. KPI (median) and chart (mean×T) are different aggregations — both correct

`stats.median_velocity_mm_yr` is the **median**; the chart is the **mean** × T — both right, never "reconcile" them.

| case | mean mm/yr (chart) | median mm/yr (KPI) | mean×T | median×T |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `mexico-city` | −85.8 | −62.1 | −31.0 mm | −22.4 mm |
| `jakarta` | −40.6 | −25.4 | −14.7 mm | −9.2 mm |
| `malaga` | −1.4 | −1.4 | −0.50 mm | −0.49 mm |

## 4. What the UI must surface from `meta.json`

`revisit_days` (12 for NISAR, 6 for Sentinel-1 — never pool coherence across them), `thresholds`
(so the coherence filter's range is explainable), `provenance.{source,method,reference,license}`,
`limitations[]` (verbatim, they are the honest caveats), `null_policy`, and `stats` for the KPI
cards — including `detection_limit_mm_yr` when it is published (§2b).

## 5. What will change when real data lands

The files are replaced, the schema is not. If a column genuinely has to change, it is a contract
change: bump `SCHEMA_VERSION`, add a `CHANGELOG` line, and get all three roles to agree — silence is
not agreement.

## 6. Questions

- Schema, units, thresholds, provenance → **yuls** (Rol 3).
- Loading, validation, filters, metrics → **pozo** (Rol 1).
- Presentation, colours, interaction → **fradiaz** (Rol 2), with yuls on legends.
